glosses: to long for, crave
~ naar: een sterk verlangen koesteren naar iets

examples.text: Zij hunkerde naar een beetje erkenning.

glosses: eine irgendwie geartete Entbehrung erleiden (insbesondere hungern und/oder dürsten)

examples.text: „Kinder von 1 bis 7 Jahren überstehen die See-Reise selten, und müssen die Eltern ihre Kinder manchmal durch Mangel, Hunger, Durst und dergleichen Zufälle elendiglich schmachten, sterben und ins Wasser geworfen sehen.“
Der grausame Ritter ließ die Gefangenen monatelang im Kerker schmachten.
Erni erzählte mir, er habe bei der Wanderung in der Hitze ganz schön geschmachtet.

glosses: sich schmerzlich nach jemandem oder nach etwas sehnen, vor Sehnsucht dahinwelken

examples.text: „Bald begannen sie ihm zuzuzwinkern und nach ihm zu schmachten, und jede einzelne von ihnen hätte sich nichts sehnlicher gewünscht, als in seinen Armen zu liegen.“
Nach dem Ausflug in die Sahara schmachtete die Reisegruppe nach Wasser.

glosses: seinen Hunger und Durst bei jemandem stillen, ohne etwas zu bezahlen

examples.text: Die Mägde des Fronherren schmachten gern an unserem Tisch.

glosses: etwas von jemandem fordern, etwas haben wollen

examples.text: Ich verlange von ihnen, dass sie ordentliche Arbeit abliefern!
Der Gast verlangt gutes Essen und Luxus von einem Fünfsternehotel.

„1933 veröffentlicht er den Aufsatz ‚Die Kirche vor der Judenfrage‘ und verlangt darin von der Kirche, nicht nur den Opfern der staatlichen Gewalt zu helfen, sondern auch aktiven Widerstand zu leisten – ‚dem Rad selbst in die Speichen fallen‘.“

glosses: etwas notwendig machen, erfordern

examples.text: Es verlangt viel Mut und Ausdauer, um an einem solchen Wettbewerb teilzunehmen.
Komm mal kurz her, du wirst am Telefon verlangt.

glosses: mit jemandem (am Telefon) sprechen wollen

examples.text: Ich verlange den Chef der Firma – ich muss unbedingt mit ihm sprechen.

glosses: jemanden oder etwas benötigen, unbedingt brauchen, bei sich haben wollen

examples.text: Die schwerkranke Person verlangt sofort einen Arzt.
Das kleine Kind verlangt seine Mutter und seinen Teddybären.
Sie verlangt nach jemandem, mit dem sie all ihre Gedanken austauschen kann.

glosses: an einen Gegenstand so herankommen, das man ihn greifen kann; erreichen

examples.text: Kannst du mir die Butter reichen? Ich verlange sie nicht.

glosses: To have a strong desire for something or to do something; to long for or to do something.

examples.text: But all that night his body yearned for Alec's, despite him. He called it lustful, a word easily uttered, and opposed it to his work, his family, his friends, his position in society. […] But his body would not be convinced.
Anne, please tell me over again that you like me a little bit. I yearn to hear it.
All I yearn for is a simple life.
I muſt do that my heart-ſtrings yern to do: but my word's paſt.
You are now before my eyes, my eyes that are ready to flow with tenderness, but cannot give relief to my gushing heart, that dictates what I am now saying, and yearns to tell you all its achings.

By morning's cheerful glow, but oftener still by evening's gentle light, the child, with a respect for the short and happy intercourse of these two sisters which forbade her to approach and say a thankful word, although she yearned to do so, followed them at a distance in their walks and rambles, […]
What his soul yearned after was control of his father's newly purchased sailing-ship.
And Jim supported his twitching body by holding on to the sink, the while he yearned toward the yellowish concoction that stood for life.

glosses: To have a strong desire for something or to do something; to long for or to do something.
To long for something in the past with melancholy or nostalgia.

examples.text: If I don’t go now, thought Charlotte, I shall have lost a chance which I shall eternally regret and yearn after.
Having shaken the dust of the ugly new South Africa from his feet, is he yearning for the South Africa of the old days, when Eden was still possible?

glosses: Of music, words, etc.: to express strong desire or longing.

examples.text: The music, yearning like a God in pain, / She scarcely heard: […]

glosses: To have strong feelings of affection, love, sympathy, etc., toward someone.

examples.text: And Joſeph made haſte: for his bowels did yerne upon his brother: and he ſought where to weepe, and hee entred into his chamber, & wept there.
I have left your mother in the next room. Her heart yearns towards you.

Oh, it was a pretty sight to see this modest young creature, little more than a child herself, anticipating maternity, but blushing every now and then, and looking askant at her lord and master. How his very bowels yearned over her!
[…] Mr. Ratcliffe’s heart yearned toward the charming girl quite with the sensations of a father, or even of an elder brother.
But supper had cheered Tant' Sannie, who found it impossible longer to maintain that decorous silence, and whose heart yearned over the youth.

glosses: To be distressed or pained; to grieve; to mourn.

examples.text: My father’s and my uncle Toby’s hearts yearn’d with ſympathy for the poor fellow’s diſtreſs,—[…]

glosses: Often followed by out: to perform (music) which conveys or say (words) which express strong desire or longing.
To have a strong desire or longing (for something or to do something).
To cause (someone) to have strong feelings of affection, love, sympathy, etc.; also, to grieve or pain (someone).

examples.text: Well, ſhe laments Sir for it, that it would yern your heart to see it: […]

It yernes me not, if men my Garments weare; / Nor care I who doth feed vpon my coſt: / Such outward things dwell not in my deſires. / But if it be a ſinne to couet Honor, / I am the moſt offending Soule aliue.
When the badger finds that the terriers yearn him in his burrow, he will stop the hole between him and the terriers; […]

glosses: A strong desire or longing; a yearning, a yen.

examples.text: Gibbs now said he wasn't going to pull any punches with Gary when he knew how jealous a man could get, so he also wanted to tell him that Phil Hansen was reputed to have a yearn for attractive ladies.

To curdle (milk), especially in the cheesemaking process.
To make (cheese) from curdled milk.

examples.text: Also his Honour the Duke will accept ane of our Dunlop cheeses, and it sall be my faut if a better was ever yearned in Lowden.

glosses: книжн., устар. хотеть пить, испытывать жажду

examples.text: Истомившиеся путники жаждут.

glosses: перен., книжн. страстно хотеть чего-то

examples.text: Жаждать любви.
Жаждать сострадания.
Шайка диверсантов оголтелых // Жаждала страну поработить.

glosses: устар. почувствовать сильное желание, сильно захотеть чего-либо
устар. чувствовать голод

examples.text: Один алчет, другой пресыщается; тот в пространнейших опочивает палатах; сей не имеет, где главы приклонить; один величается благородства титлами; другой стонет под тяжким рабства игом; у сих, по словам Давидовым, житницы исполнены, овцы многоплодны, волове толсты, нет падения оплоту их, нет вопля в стогнах их; а те ждут соскорбящих, да нет; ищут утешающих, но не обретают.

glosses: перен., устар., книжн. страстно желать чего-либо, испытывать непреодолимое стремление к чему-либо

examples.text: Те, кои, с благоговением предстоя большому барину, смотрят ему в очи раболепно и алчут предузнать мысли его, чтобы заранее угодить ему подлым таканьем.
В порыве бешенства и ужаснейших терзаний я жаждал, кипел упиться одним только взглядом, только одного взгляда алкал я…
